𝗘𝗺𝗺𝗮𝗻𝘂𝗲𝗹 𝗟𝗮𝘄𝗮𝗹 — 𝗘𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗲𝗽𝗿𝗲𝗻𝗲𝘂𝗿. 𝗦𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘆𝘁𝗲𝗹𝗹𝗲𝗿. 𝗕𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗲𝗿.

I build ventures at the intersection of technology, strategy, and impact.

Founder @ 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗼𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗻, the Content Intelligence Operating System for marketing and communications agencies serving regulated industries, so they know what will work before and after publication. We're solving the $90B problem of ineffective content strategy by giving teams the foresight to engineer campaigns that deliver measurable results.

Recognised by 𝘉𝘭𝘢𝘤𝘬𝘙𝘰𝘤𝘬, 𝘉𝘢𝘳𝘤𝘭𝘢𝘺𝘴 𝘌𝘢𝘨𝘭𝘦 𝘓𝘢𝘣𝘴, 𝘕𝘷𝘪𝘥𝘪𝘢 𝘐𝘯𝘤𝘦𝘱𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘗𝘳𝘰𝘨𝘳𝘢𝘮, 𝘚𝘢𝘢𝘚𝘵𝘰𝘤𝘬, and more. LOIs secured across North America and Europe.

Beyond the startup:
Ex-Project Manager @ 𝗟𝗼𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗖𝗵𝗮𝗺𝗽𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗖𝗜𝗖 — leading the YEA! accelerator, working with underrepresented founders aged 18–30 in partnership with Peabody to refine ideas, secure funding, and build sustainable businesses.

Board Member @ 𝗟𝗟𝗗𝗖 𝗘𝗹𝗲𝘃𝗮𝘁𝗲 — advising on major East London regeneration projects, including East Bank and NG200

Co-Founder @ 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗘𝗹𝗲𝘃𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗙𝘂𝗻𝗱 — one of the UK's first youth-led social impact ventures, distributing £80K to London's ecosystem and backing ventures like Outrunners, Fight for Peace, and Urban MBA

Across The Elevate Fund and YEA!, I've distributed over £100K in funding to support London's venture ecosystem.

If you're building in B2B SaaS, MarTech, Future of Work, or social impact, let's connect.

experience.description: Building intotheopen — the Content Intelligence Operating System for marketing and communications agencies serving regulated industries, so they know what will work before and after publication.

The London Legacy Development Corporation's Elevate Board is a youth-led advisory board made up of 18–25 year olds from the host boroughs of Hackney, Newham, Tower Hamlets and Waltham Forest. Representing diversity in age, ethnicity, gender and lived experience, the Elevate Board brings community accountability and an alternative perspective to the boardrooms shaping the future of East London.

As a board member, I provide consultancy across some of the most significant regeneration and cultural programmes in the region, including East Bank, a landmark £1.1bn cultural quarter in Stratford featuring partners such as the V&A, BBC Music Studios, Sadler's Wells, London College of Fashion (UAL) and UCL, IQL North Stratford (Hadley), and The National Gallery's NG200 project, which encompasses the renovation of the Sainsbury Wing.

In 2024, the Elevate Board launched The Elevate Fund, the UK's first youth-led social impact fund, providing equity-free grants to social-impact-focused organisations and SMEs across East London. The fund secured £125,000 from Spirit of 2012, and as a founding team member, I helped build the operational infrastructure that enabled it to launch and distribute grants at scale, reaching organisations that would otherwise have lacked access to early-stage capital.

Key contributions include:
→ Co-designed the grant distribution framework and assessment criteria, ensuring funding decisions were grounded in community insight rather than conventional investor gatekeeping
→ Contributed to governance structures that enabled a youth-led board to operate with credibility and rigour alongside institutional partners
→ Represented the perspectives of young people from East London in high-level boardroom conversations typically dominated by established stakeholders
→ Provided strategic consultancy across major regeneration initiatives, bridging the gap between large-scale development and the communities most affected by it

Elevate Youth Voice, formerly known as Legacy Youth Voice, is a volunteering programme primarily made up of 13–18 year olds, giving young people a direct voice in the planning and programming decisions shaping Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park and the surrounding area.

As a member, I contributed to a range of youth-focused initiatives across the park and wider East London, including:
→ Future Me & Future Youth — a youth summit connecting young people to employment, education and opportunity across QEOP
→ East Summer School — an annual programme delivered by East Ed, bringing together industry experts and young people from across East London to unlock creativity and develop skills
→ Additional programming and consultation initiatives spanning arts, culture and community engagement across the park

This experience laid the foundation for my later progression to the London Legacy Development Corporation's Elevate Board, where I moved from contributing a youth perspective to actively shaping strategy at a senior level.

As Junior Project Manager at Local Champions CIC, I co-led the consultancy arm of the social enterprise and delivered the Young Entrepreneurs Alliance (YEA!) accelerator across both 2024 and 2025, supporting underrepresented founders across London with funding, mentorship, and business development resources.

Across both cohorts, I managed end-to-end programme delivery across Haringey and Thamesmead, supporting 30+ founders to a 100% completion rate and overseeing the distribution of £10,000 in micro-funding to early-stage businesses. I also developed and executed promotional content and partner communications that broadened YEA!'s visibility across London, securing strategic partnerships with Peabody and Clockwise.

Key contributions include:
→ Co-led the consultancy arm alongside senior leadership, contributing to business development and client engagement beyond programme delivery
→ Coordinated logistics, scheduling, and founder support across two borough programmes simultaneously
→ Secured strategic partnerships with Peabody and Clockwise through targeted stakeholder communications
→ Achieved 100% completion rate across 30+ founders over two consecutive cohorts

As Elevate Project Officer, I supported the organisation's early-stage strategic development, with a focus on stakeholder mapping and competitive landscape analysis across the East London regeneration and social impact sectors.

Working across Microsoft Excel and Word, I developed a comprehensive stakeholder, collaborator, and competitor map that fed directly into Elevate's business strategy, helping the organisation identify partnership opportunities and position itself effectively within a complex ecosystem of landowners, developers, local authorities, and community groups.

This was a supporting project undertaken during my first term as an Elevate Board Member, giving me early exposure to the strategic infrastructure behind a growing public-sector subsidiary at the intersection of urban regeneration, youth engagement, and community investment.

As part of the Young Co-Producers Programme, coordinated by the HereUs Collective, The Lab E20, and Foundation for Future London, I was one of eight young professionals responsible for the concept, design, and delivery of the HereUs stall at the Great Get Together, an annual community event on Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park.

Working collaboratively, we designed the stall, curated a programme of interactive activities, and partnered with local artists and designers to bring our vision to life, using art and creativity to tell the story of East London's history and culture. Highlights included an interactive cockney rhyming slang activity that invited attendees to engage with the cultural heritage of the area they call home.

This role built directly on my earlier involvement with Legacy Youth Voice, where I contributed to events including Future Me, Future Youth and East Summer School, applying and developing those foundations in a creative production context.

I am delighted to recommend Emmanuel. He is not only very polite and well-dressed but also an incredibly ambitious entrepreneur. Emmanuel consistently goes above and beyond to support others, demonstrating his commitment to helping those around him succeed.

I remember we once sat in the library, and he told me about how he was going to set something up. Now, I can't stop seeing "Into the Open," which is a testament to his hard work. This shows another great aspect of his character—not just talking about it, but actually going and doing it. Emmanuel is a real grafter and go-getter.

He regularly attends my networking events, showing his dedication to growing both as a professional and as a person. Emmanuel's eagerness to learn and his proactive approach make him a standout individual in any setting.

If you're thinking about working with him or connecting, Emmanuel is the perfect person to have on your team. His drive, professionalism, and genuine care for others make him an invaluable asset.
